cards.front: Complete the rule: Use headlights whenever seeing other road users becomes.
cards.back: Use headlights whenever seeing other road users becomes difficult, so they can see your vehicle too.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If needed, briefly flash the headlights to.
cards.back: If needed, briefly flash the headlights to alert another road user to your presence.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When using windshield wipers in rain, snow.
cards.back: When using windshield wipers in rain, snow or fog, turn the headlights on as well.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Turn the headlights on.
cards.back: Turn the headlights on as daylight begins to fade.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When driving requires lights, use.
cards.back: When driving requires lights, use headlights rather than parking lights.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use headlights when driving away from a rising.
cards.back: Use headlights when driving away from a rising or setting sun to help approaching drivers see you.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use the horn when it.
cards.back: Use the horn when it can help prevent a collision.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Without immediate danger, use a light.
cards.back: Without immediate danger, use a light horn tap rather than a sharp blast.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A light horn tap can warn a pedestrian.
cards.back: A light horn tap can warn a pedestrian or bicyclist who appears to be entering your travel lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use a light horn tap if a driver.
cards.back: Use a light horn tap if a driver starts moving into your lane as you pass.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A light horn tap can alert a driver.
cards.back: A light horn tap can alert a driver who is inattentive or may not see you.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A light horn tap can announce your approach.
cards.back: A light horn tap can announce your approach where a steep hill, sharp curve or narrow alley blocks the view ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Give a sharp horn warning when a child.
cards.back: Give a sharp horn warning when a child or older person is about to enter the street on foot or by riding.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use a sharp horn warning if.
cards.back: Use a sharp horn warning if another vehicle is about to hit you.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If you lose control and are moving.
cards.back: If you lose control and are moving toward someone, use a sharp horn warning.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not sound the horn merely to.
cards.back: Do not sound the horn merely to pressure someone to go faster or move aside.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not use the horn to point out.
cards.back: Do not use the horn to point out another driver’s mistake or to greet a friend.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not use the.
cards.back: Do not use the horn around visually impaired pedestrians.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When a vehicle breaks down, use an.
cards.back: When a vehicle breaks down, use an available phone or two-way radio to notify authorities.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If vehicle trouble requires stopping, move off.
cards.back: If vehicle trouble requires stopping, move off the road and away from traffic whenever possible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Turn on emergency flashers.
cards.back: Turn on emergency flashers when stopping for vehicle trouble.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a disabled vehicle cannot leave the roadway.
cards.back: If a disabled vehicle cannot leave the roadway, stop where drivers can see it clearly rather than just beyond a hill or curve.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Place appropriate emergency warnings behind a.
cards.back: Place appropriate emergency warnings behind a stopped vehicle to alert approaching traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If no flares or warning devices are available.
cards.back: If no flares or warning devices are available, wave traffic around the vehicle from a safe place beside the road, using a white cloth if available.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Never stand in a travel lane or attempt.
cards.back: Never stand in a travel lane or attempt a tire change that would put you in one.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A raised hood or white cloth tied to.
cards.back: A raised hood or white cloth tied to an antenna, side mirror or door handle can signal an emergency.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Avoid driving beside another vehicle and slightly behind.
cards.back: Avoid driving beside another vehicle and slightly behind it where its driver may not see you.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Speed up or fall back from another vehicle’s.
cards.back: Speed up or fall back from another vehicle’s blind spot so its driver can see you more easily.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When passing, move through the other.
cards.back: When passing, move through the other driver’s blind spot as promptly as possible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not remain alongside a truck or bus.
cards.back: Do not remain alongside a truck or bus because its large blind spots make your vehicle hard to see.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Warn other drivers before changing direction or.
cards.back: Warn other drivers before changing direction or slowing so they have time to react.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Signal before changing lanes, turning.
cards.back: Signal before changing lanes, turning, merging, highway passing or parking.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Signal a direction or lane change even.
cards.back: Signal a direction or lane change even when no other road user is visible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before a left turn, check traffic behind, signal.
cards.back: Before a left turn, check traffic behind, signal and move close to the centerline well ahead of the turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a turn, signal for one hundred feet.
cards.back: For a turn, signal for one hundred feet in the city or three hundred feet in rural areas while beginning to slow.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before turning left, look for.
cards.back: Before turning left, look for oncoming traffic and yield to it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: While waiting to turn left, keep the wheels.
cards.back: While waiting to turn left, keep the wheels straight so a rear impact does not push you into oncoming traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Enter the destination street just right of its.
cards.back: Enter the destination street just right of its center when turning left, without cutting the corner.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a left turn, move gradually to the.
cards.back: After a left turn, move gradually to the middle of your lane and check that the signal is canceled.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Prepare for a right turn by selecting the.
cards.back: Prepare for a right turn by selecting the proper lane early and staying as close as practical to the right curb or roadway edge.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Complete a right turn near the right side.
cards.back: Complete a right turn near the right side without sweeping wide or crossing into the left lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a driveway, street or entrance lies before.
cards.back: If a driveway, street or entrance lies before the intended turn, pass it before signaling so others do not mistake the turning location.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a vehicle is about to enter between.
cards.back: If a vehicle is about to enter between you and the intended turn, wait until you pass it before signaling that turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a turn or lane change, cancel the.
cards.back: After a turn or lane change, cancel the signal manually if it has not canceled itself.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Begin slowing as early as.
cards.back: Begin slowing as early as it is safe to do so.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before an unexpected stop or slowdown, tap the.
cards.back: Before an unexpected stop or slowdown, tap the brake pedal quickly three or four times to warn following drivers.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Warn following traffic before slowing to leave a.
cards.back: Warn following traffic before slowing to leave a road without a separate turn or exit lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Warn following drivers when parking or turning just.
cards.back: Warn following drivers when parking or turning just before an intersection where they may expect you to continue.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Warn following drivers before slowing for a.
cards.back: Warn following drivers before slowing for a hazard or stopped traffic they cannot see.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drivers must know basic hand signals even.
cards.back: Drivers must know basic hand signals even when their vehicle has turn and brake lights.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Safe speed must account for the road.
cards.back: Safe speed must account for the road, surrounding traffic, visibility and the posted limit.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Reduce speed before a curve, on a slippery.
cards.back: Reduce speed before a curve, on a slippery surface or where water is standing on the road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Tire grip depends on both tire condition.
cards.back: Tire grip depends on both tire condition and the type and condition of the roadway.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use the owner’s manual to.
cards.back: Use the owner’s manual to find the proper tire pressure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drive more slowly on gravel or dirt because.
cards.back: Drive more slowly on gravel or dirt because reduced traction lengthens stopping and makes turning skids easier.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Washboard ruts and potholes on.
cards.back: Washboard ruts and potholes on gravel can affect steering and control.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Low-beam headlights are recommended in gravel-road.
cards.back: Low-beam headlights are recommended in gravel-road dust to make the vehicle more visible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On narrow dirt or gravel roads, watch for.
cards.back: On narrow dirt or gravel roads, watch for narrow-bridge warnings and be prepared to stop for oncoming traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slow before entering a curve, because braking.
cards.back: Slow before entering a curve, because braking during the curve can cause a skid.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At the first rain, snow or sleet, slow.
cards.back: At the first rain, snow or sleet, slow because the tires have less grip than on a dry road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On a wet road, the handbook advises.
cards.back: On a wet road, the handbook advises reducing speed by about ten miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On packed snow, the handbook.
cards.back: On packed snow, the handbook advises cutting speed in half.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use snow tires or chains.
cards.back: Use snow tires or chains when the road is snow-covered.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On ice, slow to a.
cards.back: On ice, slow to a crawl and avoid driving if possible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If stranded in a snowstorm, remaining in.
cards.back: If stranded in a snowstorm, remaining in the car makes being found more likely.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Shaded areas can become icy first.
cards.back: Shaded areas can become icy first and dry last on cold, wet days.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Bridge pavement may be icy even.
cards.back: Bridge pavement may be icy even where nearby road pavement is not.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Ice near freezing can be wetter and.
cards.back: Ice near freezing can be wetter and more slippery than ice at much colder temperatures.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Early rain on a hot road may.
cards.back: Early rain on a hot road may be especially slippery until surface oil washes away.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a.
cards.back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a film of water instead of gripping the road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slowing on wet roads is the.
cards.back: Slowing on wet roads is the handbook’s main advice for avoiding hydroplaning.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the tires seem to lose road.
cards.back: If the tires seem to lose road contact in water, ease off the accelerator.

cards.front: Complete the rule: During hydroplaning, keep the steering straight unless an.
cards.back: During hydroplaning, keep the steering straight unless an emergency requires turning, and make any necessary turn slowly.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Wait for tire grip to return.
cards.back: Wait for tire grip to return before ordinary braking or turning after hydroplaning.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A skid begins when the tires.
cards.back: A skid begins when the tires can no longer grip the roadway.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the vehicle starts sliding, release the accelerator.
cards.back: If the vehicle starts sliding, release the accelerator and look toward the direction you want to travel.

cards.front: Complete the rule: While a sliding vehicle slows, stay off the.
cards.back: While a sliding vehicle slows, stay off the brake as directed in the handbook’s skid-recovery sequence.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In skid recovery, steer toward the desired path.
cards.back: In skid recovery, steer toward the desired path, then reverse the steering correction as soon as the vehicle straightens.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep correcting the steering during skid recovery until.
cards.back: Keep correcting the steering during skid recovery until the vehicle travels down the road under control again.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Watch for wildlife especially around sunrise and sunset.
cards.back: Watch for wildlife especially around sunrise and sunset, and slow with readiness to stop if an animal appears.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If there is no time to stop or.
cards.back: If there is no time to stop or avoid an animal, do not make a sharp swerve.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After seeing a deer, elk or.
cards.back: After seeing a deer, elk or similar herd animal, watch for more animals.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drive with surrounding traffic.
cards.back: Drive with surrounding traffic and pass only when needed.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If vehicles pile up behind your slower vehicle.
cards.back: If vehicles pile up behind your slower vehicle, pull over to let them pass when it is safe.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When merging, signal, use the rearview.
cards.back: When merging, signal, use the rearview mirror and look over your shoulder.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use an acceleration ramp to approach the.
cards.back: Use an acceleration ramp to approach the traffic speed before joining the main road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not drive to the ramp’s end and.
cards.back: Do not drive to the ramp’s end and stop; if waiting for a gap is necessary, slow earlier to retain acceleration room.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On a controlled-access highway, move left when.
cards.back: On a controlled-access highway, move left when possible to help another driver enter safely.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With an exit ramp, signal first and delay.
cards.back: With an exit ramp, signal first and delay slowing until the vehicle is on the ramp.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When leaving a fast two-lane road with traffic.
cards.back: When leaving a fast two-lane road with traffic behind, avoid slowing too early, tap the brakes and reduce speed promptly but safely.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Watch for trucks and underpowered cars that may.
cards.back: Watch for trucks and underpowered cars that may lose speed on steep grades or need longer to enter traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and road-maintenance vehicles usually.
cards.back: Farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and road-maintenance vehicles usually travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less and need a rear slow-moving sign.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A slow-moving vehicle must turn off when it.
cards.back: A slow-moving vehicle must turn off when it delays four or more vehicles and sufficient room permits a safe turnout.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slow-moving traffic must use.
cards.back: Slow-moving traffic must use the extreme right lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Reduce speed in crowded places where people.
cards.back: Reduce speed in crowded places where people and traffic leave little room to maneuver.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Be ready to slow around shopping areas, parking.
cards.back: Be ready to slow around shopping areas, parking lots, busy downtown streets, rush traffic, narrow bridges, tunnels and toll plazas.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Around schools, playgrounds and residential streets.
cards.back: Around schools, playgrounds and residential streets, watch for children entering without looking.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With good tires, working brakes and dry pavement.
cards.back: With good tires, working brakes and dry pavement, reacting and stopping from fifty miles per hour can take about four hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With good tires, working brakes and dry pavement.
cards.back: With good tires, working brakes and dry pavement, stopping from thirty miles per hour can take about two hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Choose a nighttime speed that lets.
cards.back: Choose a nighttime speed that lets you stop within the distance illuminated ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In rain, fog or snow, use headlights.
cards.back: In rain, fog or snow, use headlights so other drivers can see the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In very heavy rain, thick fog or a.
cards.back: In very heavy rain, thick fog or a snowstorm that limits the view to about two hundred feet, the handbook warns that more than thirty miles per hour is unsafe.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a downpour prevents adequate vision for driving.
cards.back: If a downpour prevents adequate vision for driving, pull off safely and wait for the weather to clear.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Approach a hill or curve with blocked sightlines.
cards.back: Approach a hill or curve with blocked sightlines slowly enough to stop for a hidden obstruction.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Give parked vehicles as much room as possible.
cards.back: Give parked vehicles as much room as possible because they can hide pedestrians or people getting out.
